redisTemplate.value_and_hash_value_serializers: Public JDK defaults, with no native setter override.

cacheManager.TTL: Default eternal TTL (Duration.ZERO); no new TTL override.

original_contract.redisCacheWriter: nonLockingRedisCacheWriter(factory), already matching current owned implementation; unchanged.
original_contract.RedisKeySerializer: Original source extends StringRedisSerializer, prepends spring.redis.namespace (default empty), and in tenant profile appends the existing tenant suffix once. Separate original constructor calls remain separate; no shared singleton added.

prior_owned_difference.template: No key/hash-key override after afterPropertiesSet, leaving JDK-serialized keys.
prior_owned_difference.cacheManager: Default String-serialized cache keys and cached nulls enabled.
prior_owned_difference.business_effect: CacheManager writes String layout cache keys. Original RedisHelper bulk eviction scans those raw String keys, then calls RedisTemplate.delete(Collection); the prior template serializes the scanned Strings as different JDK byte keys, so the actual layout entry survives a successful panel update.

source_causal_chain.meaning: Original @Cacheable core-user-panel-config-layout uses user/role key generator and copies panel title/URL/config to the cached representation.
Raw SCAN by cacheName::* -> String key set -> RedisTemplate.delete(keySet).
delete(Collection) calls rawKeys/rawKey with the template key serializer; default initialization uses JdkSerializationRedisSerializer.

measured_cycle.purpose: Warm dedicated panel layout with title A.
Change original panel title to B.
Read actual persisted title B on both sides.
Owned still returns cached A while supplier returns B.

diagnostic_http_before.interpretation: The original update persisted B in both runtimes, while only owned returned stale layout A. This is a source-backed cache eviction compatibility failure rather than a failed write, response-only inference or different test record.
diagnostic_http_before.GET_side_effect_boundary: Original layouts may initialize scheme rows when absent. The measurement uses already-created dedicated personal schemes; setup and cleanup HTTP writes remain explicit.
diagnostic_http_before.not_strict: This real HTTP reproduction is diagnostic; it does not establish the post-repair outcome or promote API strict evidence.

business_zero.scope: Both earlier owned-only failed attempts and the final owned/supplier reproduction are retained and checked.

exact_layout_cache_zero.scope: Authenticated exact existence reads for three dedicated fixture cache keys per side; cache values were not read.

invalid_scan_retained.reason: Original SCAN cursor was incomplete and supplier returned NOAUTH. Its original error fields remain; only subsequent authenticated exact-key reads establish cache absence.

fixture_cleanup_before.restoration: HTTP restore title A and API fixture removal are compensation, not a demonstrated transaction rollback. Original empty personal-layout PUT performs exact user-scope @CacheEvict before final deletion. Monotonic sequence allocations remain retained.
fixture_cleanup_before.audit_limitation: Existing preflight reports auditTrail disabled for USER and workspace scheme; this reproduction does not claim complete audit or transaction rollback acceptance.

public_dependency.configuration_defaults: String key serializer and JDK value serializer in default RedisCacheConfiguration; JDK key/hash-key defaults in RedisTemplate without explicit overrides.

replacement.behavior: Restore original key/hash-key RedisKeySerializer constructors after template initialization, and original no-null/cache-key configuration for CacheManager. Keep all value serializers, TTL, prefix, writer, native-removal boundaries and business source unchanged.
replacement.startup: RedisKeySerializer reads the existing ApplicationContextHelper Environment. ApplicationConfiguration already initializes that helper in its PostConstruct before its bean methods; no new lifecycle or context facade is added.

analysis_method: Complete exact-symbol native disassembly without execution
Original private class hashes and reconstructed serializer/helper/business source
Byte-identical public Spring Data Redis bytecode
Existing real HTTP dedicated fixture reproduction and precise business/cache cleanup reads
limitations: No after-repair HTTP success is recorded in this provenance; source repair outcome remains to be verified against the same business loop.
Workspace layout excludes null via its own unless expression; this reproduction specifically proves key/eviction behavior, not every cached-null contract.
Existing nonempty namespace/tenant raw SCAN behavior is not redesigned here; observed fixture uses the reviewed non-tenant/default-namespace configuration.

Changing key serializers does not migrate old JDK-keyed sessions/RSA/captcha entries. No Redis flush, broad deletion or generic migration is part of this repair; fresh authenticated sessions may be required.
No private supplier class or native artifact is added to the final runtime, and no extra process/runtime is introduced.
